questions.question: What problem does the Lakehouse architecture solve?
options: It removes the need for any storage
It combines the low-cost open storage of a data lake with the reliability and performance of a data warehouse
questions.explanation: The lakehouse unifies lake and warehouse so one platform serves both BI and data science on open storage.

questions.question: In Databricks, what does 'serverless' compute mean for you?
options: You must buy your own servers
It runs only on your laptop
Compute is provisioned and managed automatically — you don't create or size clusters
questions.explanation: Serverless removes cluster management; Databricks provisions and scales compute for you.

questions.question: What does Databricks Free Edition cost?
options: Nothing — it is free, with no credit card required
questions.explanation: Free Edition is permanently free and needs no cloud account or card.

questions.question: In a Python notebook, how do you run a SQL statement in a cell?
options: Start the cell with the %sql magic
You cannot mix SQL and Python
questions.explanation: The %sql magic switches a single cell to SQL against the same tables.

questions.question: Which is designed to run analytical SQL queries and dashboards?
questions.explanation: SQL warehouses are the compute behind Databricks SQL and AI/BI dashboards.

questions.question: What is the correct order of Unity Catalog's three-level namespace?
questions.explanation: Objects are addressed as catalog.schema.table.

questions.question: What is a Unity Catalog Volume used for?
options: Governed storage of non-tabular files (e.g. raw CSV/JSON)
questions.explanation: Volumes hold files under Unity Catalog governance, e.g. a raw landing zone.

questions.question: How does a managed table differ from an external table?
options: Databricks manages the underlying storage lifecycle of a managed table
questions.explanation: For managed tables Databricks controls the data files; external tables point at storage you manage.

questions.question: Why keep your cohort project in a Git folder?
options: For version control, history, and reproducible collaboration
questions.explanation: Git folders connect the workspace to GitHub so work is versioned and submittable.

questions.question: What is a metastore in Unity Catalog?
options: The top-level container that holds catalogs and their metadata
questions.explanation: The metastore is the root of the governance hierarchy for an account/region.

questions.question: Which of these is an action (not a transformation) in Spark?
questions.explanation: Actions like count()/show()/collect() trigger execution; the others are lazy transformations.

questions.question: What does 'lazy evaluation' mean in Spark?
options: Transformations are not executed until an action is called
questions.explanation: Spark builds a plan and only computes when an action requires a result.

questions.question: What does createOrReplaceTempView let you do?
questions.explanation: A temp view exposes a DataFrame to Spark SQL for %sql cells.

questions.question: Which transformation causes a shuffle across the cluster?
options: A narrow transformation such as filter
A wide transformation such as groupBy
questions.explanation: Wide transformations redistribute data (shuffle); narrow ones stay within a partition.

questions.question: What is the Databricks Assistant?
options: A built-in AI helper that explains and generates code
questions.explanation: The Assistant is your free in-notebook AI pair-programmer.

questions.question: What does the Bronze layer of the medallion architecture hold?
questions.explanation: Bronze preserves raw fidelity; cleaning happens later in Silver.

questions.question: What is the Gold layer for?
options: Business-ready, aggregated data for analytics and BI
questions.explanation: Gold serves curated metrics and star-schema tables to consumers.

questions.question: Why do you use synthetic data in this cohort?
options: Because Databricks can't read real data
To avoid handling real member PHI while still practising on realistic data
questions.explanation: Synthetic data keeps the exercise safe and compliant — never real records.

questions.question: What is the correct medallion order?
questions.explanation: Data flows raw (Bronze) to cleaned (Silver) to business-ready (Gold).

questions.question: Where do the raw claims files land in this project?
questions.explanation: Raw files are written to the bronze.raw Volume as a landing zone.

questions.question: What gives Delta Lake its ACID guarantees?
questions.explanation: Delta's transaction log records atomic, ordered commits enabling ACID.

questions.question: What does Delta time travel let you do?
options: Query a previous version of a table
questions.explanation: You can read older versions with VERSION AS OF / TIMESTAMP AS OF.

questions.question: What does schema enforcement do?
options: Rejects writes whose schema doesn't match the table
questions.explanation: Delta blocks mismatched writes unless you explicitly evolve the schema.

questions.question: Why choose Delta over plain CSV/Parquet?
options: It is the only format Spark reads
It adds ACID transactions, versioning, and schema management
It removes the need for tables
questions.explanation: Delta layers reliability features on top of Parquet.

questions.question: What does the mergeSchema option allow?
options: Adding new columns to a table on write
questions.explanation: mergeSchema evolves the schema to accept new columns.

questions.question: What is the guiding principle of the Bronze layer?
options: Keep the data raw and append-only, adding only metadata
questions.explanation: Bronze preserves raw data; transformation is Silver's job.

questions.question: What does input_file_name() return?
options: The path of the source file for each row
questions.explanation: It's used to record source-file lineage in Bronze.

questions.question: Why add ingestion metadata columns?
options: For lineage and debugging (which file, when, which batch)
questions.explanation: _source_file/_ingested_at/_batch_id trace where and when data arrived.

questions.question: What does 'append-only Bronze' imply?
options: You delete old rows each run
You add new data without overwriting or cleaning it
questions.explanation: Bronze accumulates raw records; cleaning is deferred to Silver.

questions.question: What is current_timestamp() typically used for in Bronze?
questions.explanation: It stamps each row with when it was ingested.

questions.question: What is 'cloudFiles' in Databricks?
options: The format string that enables Auto Loader for incremental ingestion
questions.explanation: spark.readStream.format('cloudFiles') is Auto Loader.

questions.question: What do Auto Loader checkpoints guarantee?
questions.explanation: Checkpoints track processed files so re-runs don't reprocess.

questions.question: What does the _rescued_data column capture?
options: Data that didn't match the inferred schema
questions.explanation: Rescued data preserves values that don't fit the current schema.

questions.question: What does the availableNow trigger do?
options: Processes all new files then stops (batch-style incremental)
questions.explanation: availableNow gives incremental semantics in a batch run.

questions.question: What is schema evolution in Auto Loader?
options: New columns in incoming files are handled automatically
It requires manual DDL every time
questions.explanation: Auto Loader can evolve the schema as new fields appear.

questions.question: Converting a string like '2026-01-01' to a date type is called…
questions.explanation: Casting changes a column's data type.

questions.question: What does dropDuplicates() do?
questions.explanation: It deduplicates rows, optionally on chosen keys.

questions.question: Why standardize values like state codes to a single case?
options: So joins, filters, and grouping behave consistently
questions.explanation: Consistent formatting prevents mismatches downstream.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Silver layer?
questions.explanation: Silver turns raw Bronze into trustworthy, conformed tables.

questions.question: A window function is often used to…
options: Keep the latest record per key (partition + order)
questions.explanation: Windowing by key/order enables 'keep latest' deduplication.

questions.question: A LEFT join returns…
options: All rows from the left table plus matching right rows
questions.explanation: Left joins preserve every left row, filling nulls where no match.

questions.question: What does an ANTI-join return?
options: Left rows that have no match on the right
questions.explanation: Anti-joins are ideal for finding orphan/unmatched records.

questions.question: Why derive a boolean like is_denied?
options: To make filtering and metrics simple and fast
questions.explanation: Precomputed flags simplify KPI queries.

questions.question: After a join, two columns share a name. What's the fix?
options: Alias or explicitly select the columns you want
questions.explanation: Disambiguate by aliasing or selecting specific columns.

questions.question: A referential-integrity check on claims finds…
options: Orphan claims whose member or provider doesn't exist
questions.explanation: Anti-joining to dimensions surfaces orphans.

questions.question: What is the 'quarantine' pattern?
options: Routing failing rows to a separate table instead of dropping them silently
questions.explanation: Quarantine keeps bad rows visible for review.

questions.question: A Delta CHECK constraint…
options: Rejects inserts that violate a rule at the table level
questions.explanation: CHECK constraints enforce data rules in the table itself.

questions.question: The 'completeness' data-quality dimension checks for…
questions.explanation: Completeness is about whether required values are present.

questions.question: Why not silently drop rows that fail rules?
options: You lose visibility into data problems
questions.explanation: Silent drops hide quality issues; quarantining preserves them.

questions.question: 'Validity' as a quality dimension means…
options: Values fall within an allowed set or range
questions.explanation: E.g. status must be one of paid/denied/pending.

questions.question: What does MERGE INTO do?
options: Insert, update, and delete in a single statement (upsert)
questions.explanation: MERGE performs conditional upserts against a target table.

questions.question: SCD Type 1 handles a change by…
questions.explanation: Type 1 simply overwrites.

questions.question: SCD Type 2 handles a change by…
options: Keeping history with effective_from/effective_to and a current flag
questions.explanation: Type 2 preserves historical versions.

questions.question: What does an is_current column indicate?
options: Which row is the active/current version
questions.explanation: is_current marks the live record in an SCD Type 2 table.

questions.question: Why is an upsert made idempotent?
options: So re-running it doesn't create duplicates
questions.explanation: Idempotency lets pipelines safely retry.

questions.question: What problem does OPTIMIZE address?
options: The small-files problem, by compacting files
questions.explanation: OPTIMIZE compacts many small files into fewer larger ones.

questions.question: Liquid clustering / Z-ORDER improves…
options: Data skipping for faster filtered queries
questions.explanation: Clustering co-locates related data so queries scan less.

questions.question: What does VACUUM do?
questions.explanation: VACUUM cleans up files beyond the retention window.

questions.question: What's the trade-off when you VACUUM aggressively?
options: You shorten how far back time travel can go
questions.explanation: Removing old files limits time-travel history.

questions.question: Why do many small files hurt performance?
questions.explanation: Compaction reduces file-handling overhead.

questions.question: In a star schema, the fact table stores…
options: Measures at a defined grain (e.g. amounts per claim)
questions.explanation: Facts hold numeric measures and foreign keys to dimensions.

questions.question: A dimension table stores…
questions.explanation: Dimensions describe the 'who/what/when' around facts.

questions.question: What is the 'grain' of a fact table?
options: The level of detail one fact row represents
questions.explanation: Deciding grain (e.g. one row per claim) is the first modeling step.

questions.question: What shape defines a star schema?
options: A central fact table surrounded by dimension tables
questions.explanation: Facts in the center, dimensions radiating out.

questions.question: Why include a dedicated date dimension?
options: To support flexible time-based analysis (year, quarter, weekday)
questions.explanation: A date dimension standardizes calendar attributes for BI.

questions.question: What is a surrogate key?
options: A system-generated unique identifier for a dimension row
questions.explanation: Surrogate keys decouple the warehouse from source keys.

questions.question: Why generate a dim_date programmatically?
options: To get consistent calendar attributes for every date
questions.explanation: A generated calendar table powers time analysis.

questions.question: A 'conformed' dimension is…
questions.explanation: Conformed dimensions give consistent meaning across the model.

questions.question: age_band on dim_member is an example of…
questions.explanation: Derived attributes bucket raw values for analysis.

questions.question: Why include only BI-relevant attributes in a dimension?
questions.explanation: Lean dimensions are easier and faster to consume.

questions.question: A fact table links to dimensions using…
questions.explanation: Facts store the dimensions' surrogate keys.

questions.question: Which is an additive measure?
questions.explanation: Additive measures can be summed across dimensions.

questions.question: How are claims with no matching member handled?
options: Routed to an 'Unknown' dimension member instead of dropped
questions.explanation: An Unknown member preserves the fact without losing it.

questions.question: Why reconcile fact totals against Silver?
options: To confirm the fact was built correctly
questions.explanation: Totals must match the trusted Silver source.

questions.question: Maintaining fact grain integrity means…
options: Exactly one row per defined grain
questions.explanation: Grain integrity keeps aggregations correct.

questions.question: Denial rate is best defined as…
options: Denied claims divided by total claims
questions.explanation: It's a ratio of denied to total claims.

questions.question: What does PMPM stand for?
questions.explanation: PMPM is a core healthcare cost metric.

questions.question: How does a view differ from a materialized view?
options: A materialized view is slower always
A view computes on read; a materialized view stores precomputed results
questions.explanation: Materialized views trade storage for faster reads.

questions.question: Why define KPIs precisely before building them?
options: So reporting is consistent and unambiguous
questions.explanation: Clear definitions prevent conflicting metrics.

questions.question: What is vw_claims_analytics intended for?
options: A readable, joined view for analysts
questions.explanation: It exposes an analyst-friendly shape over the star schema.

questions.question: Delta Live Tables is now called…
questions.explanation: DLT was rebranded to Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines.

questions.question: What does 'declarative ETL' mean?
options: You write every scheduler by hand
You describe the desired result and the engine manages execution
questions.explanation: Declarative pipelines let the engine handle orchestration and incrementality.

questions.question: Which is used to ingest streaming data in a pipeline?
questions.explanation: Streaming tables ingest; materialized views transform.

questions.question: What does the @dp.table decorator do?
options: Defines a dataset in a Lakeflow pipeline
questions.explanation: Decorators declare pipeline datasets (legacy @dlt still works).

questions.question: How many active pipelines per type does Free Edition allow?
questions.explanation: Free Edition permits a single active pipeline per type.

questions.question: How does a Lakeflow pipeline determine run order?
options: It auto-builds the dependency graph (DAG) from dataset references
questions.explanation: Referencing one dataset from another builds the DAG automatically.

questions.question: A materialized view in a pipeline is…
questions.explanation: Materialized views hold transform results and refresh incrementally.

questions.question: You chain Silver to Bronze by…
options: Reading the Bronze dataset from within the Silver definition
questions.explanation: Datasets reference upstream datasets to form the flow.

questions.question: What does incremental processing mean here?
options: Only new/changed data is processed on each run
questions.explanation: Incremental refresh avoids full recomputation.

questions.question: A benefit of one pipeline for the whole medallion is…
options: Managed lineage and coordinated refresh across layers
questions.explanation: A single pipeline coordinates Bronze→Silver→Gold.

questions.question: What does the expect_or_drop expectation do?
options: Drops rows that fail the rule
questions.explanation: expect_or_drop removes bad rows while continuing.

questions.question: What does expect_or_fail do?
options: Fails the pipeline update when the rule is violated
questions.explanation: expect_or_fail stops the run on violations.

questions.question: Unity Catalog lineage shows…
options: Where data comes from and where it flows, table- and column-level
questions.explanation: Lineage traces data end to end for trust and debugging.

questions.question: Where do pipeline data-quality metrics appear?
questions.explanation: Expectation pass/fail counts surface in the event log.

questions.question: Why trace lineage for a KPI?
options: To build trust and debug where a number came from
questions.explanation: Lineage lets you verify a metric back to raw.

questions.question: A 'full refresh' of a pipeline…
questions.explanation: Full refresh recomputes everything.

questions.question: An 'incremental refresh'…
options: Processes only new or changed data
questions.explanation: Incremental is the efficient default for steady-state runs.

questions.question: Parameterizing a pipeline enables…
options: Reuse across dev and prod with different config
questions.explanation: Parameters make pipelines portable and testable.

questions.question: Splitting a pipeline into modular files improves…
questions.explanation: Modular bronze/silver/gold files are easier to manage.

questions.question: Testing transforms on a sample first…
options: Catches errors cheaply before full runs
questions.explanation: Sampling reduces cost and speeds iteration.

questions.question: Databricks Workflows is now called…
questions.explanation: Workflows was rebranded to Lakeflow Jobs.

questions.question: A Lakeflow Job is…
options: A DAG of tasks with dependencies
questions.explanation: Jobs orchestrate multiple tasks in order.

questions.question: A task dependency ensures…
options: Tasks run in the correct order
questions.explanation: Dependencies encode execution order.

questions.question: A schedule on a job…
options: Triggers automatic runs at set times
questions.explanation: Schedules automate recurring runs.

questions.question: How many concurrent job tasks does Free Edition allow?
questions.explanation: Free Edition caps concurrent job tasks at 5.

questions.question: A 'task value' is used to…
options: Pass data from one task to another
questions.explanation: Task values hand small outputs downstream.

questions.question: A conditional (if/else) task…
options: Branches the job based on a condition
questions.explanation: Conditionals let the job take different paths.

questions.question: Why configure retries on a task?
options: To recover from transient failures automatically
questions.explanation: Retries handle flaky, temporary errors.

questions.question: A timeout on a task prevents…
options: A hung task from running indefinitely
questions.explanation: Timeouts bound how long a task may run.

questions.question: A file-arrival trigger runs the job when…
options: A new file lands in a monitored location
questions.explanation: File-arrival triggers react to new data.

questions.question: What does databricks.yml define?
options: A Databricks Asset Bundle (resources as code)
questions.explanation: The bundle manifest declares jobs, pipelines, and config.

questions.question: What does 'databricks bundle validate' do?
questions.explanation: Validation catches errors pre-deploy.

questions.question: Databricks Asset Bundles primarily enable…
options: Version-controlled, reproducible deployment of Databricks resources
questions.explanation: DABs package project resources as deployable code.

questions.question: A dev vs prod 'target' in a bundle represents…
questions.explanation: Targets let one bundle deploy to multiple environments.

questions.question: Why package the project as code?
questions.explanation: Code-defined infra can be reviewed and redeployed reliably.

questions.question: What does the GRANT statement do?
options: Gives a principal a privilege on an object
questions.explanation: GRANT assigns privileges like SELECT.

questions.question: 'Least privilege' means…
options: Giving only the minimum access needed
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits risk by default.

questions.question: In this project, analysts are granted…
questions.explanation: Analysts see curated Gold, not raw layers.

questions.question: The Unity Catalog privilege hierarchy is…
questions.explanation: Privileges cascade down the object hierarchy.

questions.question: What does SHOW GRANTS return?
options: The privileges granted on an object
questions.explanation: SHOW GRANTS lists who can do what.

questions.question: Column-level lineage lets you…
options: Trace a specific column back to its source
questions.explanation: UC lineage works at both table and column level.

questions.question: Why tag columns like member name and DOB?
options: To classify sensitive/PHI data for governance and discovery
questions.explanation: Tags drive classification and searchability.

questions.question: AI-generated comments in Catalog Explorer…
questions.explanation: AI suggestions speed up documentation.

questions.question: Catalog Explorer is mainly used for…
questions.explanation: It's the browse/search/govern surface for UC.

questions.question: A data dictionary documents…
questions.explanation: It's the reference describing your data.

questions.question: A column mask…
options: Redacts a column's values for unauthorized users
questions.explanation: Masks hide sensitive values by group.

questions.question: A row filter…
options: Restricts which rows a principal can see
questions.explanation: Row filters enforce row-level security.

questions.question: is_account_group_member() is used to…
options: Check a user's group membership in a dynamic view
questions.explanation: It powers per-user masking/filtering logic.

questions.question: A dynamic view…
options: Applies masking/filtering logic based on who is querying
questions.explanation: Dynamic views tailor results to the caller.

questions.question: Why are these controls critical for healthcare data?
options: They protect PHI from unauthorized access
questions.explanation: Row/column security is essential for PHI compliance.

questions.question: A Databricks SQL warehouse is…
options: Serverless compute for running SQL queries
questions.explanation: Warehouses run Databricks SQL and dashboards.

questions.question: A SQL alert…
options: Notifies you when a metric crosses a threshold
questions.explanation: Alerts watch a query result on a schedule.

questions.question: A query parameter…
options: Makes a saved query reusable with different inputs
questions.explanation: Parameters let one query serve many cases.

questions.question: A saved query can be…
questions.explanation: Saved queries are reusable and schedulable.

questions.question: A benefit of serverless SQL is…
options: No cluster management for the analyst
questions.explanation: Serverless removes infra overhead for SQL users.

questions.question: An AI/BI dashboard is built on top of…
questions.explanation: Dashboards visualize datasets defined on your data.

questions.question: A KPI tile shows…
options: A single key metric at a glance
questions.explanation: KPI tiles surface headline numbers like denial rate.

questions.question: A dashboard filter enables…
questions.explanation: Filters let viewers explore interactively.

questions.question: Publishing a dashboard…
options: Shares it, typically view-only, with stakeholders
questions.explanation: Publishing distributes the dashboard to viewers.

questions.question: A .lvdash.json file is…
options: The exported definition of an AI/BI dashboard
questions.explanation: Exporting captures the dashboard as committable JSON.

questions.question: AI/BI Genie lets stakeholders…
options: Ask questions of the data in natural language
questions.explanation: Genie translates plain English to SQL over curated data.

questions.question: Adding instructions to a Genie space…
options: Improves accuracy and grounding of answers
questions.explanation: Instructions encode definitions and business rules.

questions.question: Why verify the SQL Genie generates?
options: Natural-language-to-SQL can be wrong or ambiguous
questions.explanation: Human verification builds trust in Genie answers.

questions.question: A Genie space is grounded on…
options: Curated tables and views (your Gold layer)
questions.explanation: Grounding on curated data keeps answers relevant.

questions.question: Certified sample questions are…
options: Trusted example questions that guide Genie
questions.explanation: They steer Genie toward reliable answers.

questions.question: Scheduling a dashboard lets you…
options: Auto-refresh and email stakeholders on a cadence
questions.explanation: Subscriptions keep stakeholders updated automatically.

questions.question: The main cost driver on serverless is…
questions.explanation: You pay for compute time; idle-efficient design saves money.

questions.question: Result caching improves…
questions.explanation: Caching avoids recomputing identical queries.

questions.question: Dashboard permissions control…
options: Who can view or edit the dashboard
questions.explanation: Permissions govern access to the published asset.

questions.question: Adding an aggregate table can…
questions.explanation: Pre-aggregation reduces per-view computation.

questions.question: What is the correct end-to-end flow of your Lakehouse?
options: Raw → Bronze → Silver → Gold → pipeline → job → BI
questions.explanation: Data flows from raw ingestion through the medallion to BI.

questions.question: A retrospective captures…
options: What worked, what was hard, and what you'd change
questions.explanation: Retros turn experience into improvement.

questions.question: A good v2 roadmap for this project includes…
options: Streaming ingestion and an ML denial-prediction model
questions.explanation: The roadmap extends into ML and streaming.

questions.question: Showing lineage in the demo proves…
options: A dashboard KPI can be traced back to the raw file
questions.explanation: Lineage demonstrates end-to-end trust.

questions.question: Why require a compliance review before using real PHI?
options: Real member data carries legal and privacy obligations (e.g. HIPAA)
questions.explanation: This cohort is technical practice, not compliance sign-off.
